sentences.text: This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the injuries caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. Brief case of the petitioner in the nutshell:
It is the case of the petitioner that, on 01.10.2014 at about 7.00 p.m, when the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-HT-9866 on Geleyarabalaga road, Mahalakshmi Layout and stopped the motorcycle at junction of the Rajajinagara while the petitioner was moving his motorcycle, after getting the green signal he started his motorcycle towards right side

, at that time the driver of Indica car bearing Reg.No.KA-13-B- 4541 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner so as SCCH-23 to endanger human life and dashed to the vehicle of the petitioner and because of the said accident the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries all over his body.
It is further urged that, petitioner has spent huge amount towards hospital, transport and other incidental expenses.

It is further urged that at the time of accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, he was skilled worker and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m and due to injury the petitioner is suffering emotionally and economically and hence prayed to grant compensation amount.
The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending car and as such, the respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Contending the above facts, he prayed to grant for compensation with interest and cost.
3. Prior to remand, notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence he was placed exparte.

4. Prior to remand, after service of notice, respondent No.2 spurred in rush to the Court by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
The respondent No.2 admitting the issuance of SCCH-23 insurance policy in respect of Indica car bearing Reg.No.KA-13-B-4541.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Negligence on the part of the driver of its insured car is denied by this respondent.

Per contra it is alleged that the accident has taken place due to the negligence of the petitioner / rider of the motorcycle, as such the petitioner was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.

It is also urged that there is inordinate delay of 3 months 12 days in lodging the complaint that itself vibrantly discloses that the case is foisted so as to wangle the compensation amount from the insurance company.
The petition is bad for non- joinder of necessary parties.
Non -compliance of section's 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act is pleaded.

Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the car did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date Hemanta Kumar K vs Vijayakumar A B on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194723581/
2 of accident.

On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by SCCH-23 the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. After conclusion of the trial my Learned Predecessor-in-office had dismissed the instant petition.
Aggrieved by it, the petitioner herein preferred an appeal before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.5232/2017 (M.V-I) which was allowed.

Consequently, the judgment & award passed by this Tribunal on 20.07.2013 was set-side and the case was remanded to reconsider the matter afresh after providing reasonable opportunity to the both the parties to lead further evidence.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES

2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as claimed?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
SCCH-23 3) What order or award ?

sentences.text: ISSUE NO.1 :
The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation of an amount to the tune of Rs.10,00,000/- together.
The case of the petitioner lies an narrow compass as to claiming of compensation amount for injuries sustained by her in a Road Traffic Accident.
11. This case is remanded back by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.5232/2017 for fresh consideration after providing reasonable opportunity to the both the parties to lead further evidence.
Before dwelling into analyzing the disputed facts in issue it is relevant to have the birds eye view of the case of petitioner in a nutshell.

12. It is further urged that, petitioner has spent huge amount towards hospital, transport and other incidental expenses.

It is further urged that at the time of accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, he was skilled worker and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m and due to injury the petitioner is suffering emotionally and economically and hence prayed to grant compensation amount.
The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending car and as such, the respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Contending the above facts, he prayed to grant for compensation with interest and cost.

13. In order to substantiate the contentions of the petitioner, the petitioner himself stepped into the witness box and filed his affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in- chief as PW1 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P19 documents.
Further the petitioner has also got examined one Ragu.Y.C who is the MRT of Fortis hospital as PW2 and got marked Ex.P.20 to 22.

14. Repelling to the contentions urged by the petitioners, the respondent No.1 had attacked the case of the petitioner on various prisms known to fact and law.

It is the specific contention of respondent No.1 is that, there is in ordinate delay of more than 3 months 10 days and the insured vehicle is implanted in this case in active collusion with one respondent No.1 and the petitioner have twisted the entire episode with an oblique motive to wangle compensation.

sentences.text: In support of these contentions the respondent No.2 got examined Administrative Officer of respondent No.2 company is examined as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 document.
In order to falsify the defence of the respondent No.2 and to substantiate the case of the petitioner, petitioner counsel had cross-examined RW.1 at length 16.

On marshaling of factual matrix, on dissection of evidence placed on record and after hearing on erudite counsel appearing for combating parties, this Tribunal SCCH-23 opines that this issue is pregmented with inner issues such as :
1) Whether the delay of 3 months 10 days is fatal of the case of the petitioner ?
2) Whether the insured vehicle was implanted in this petition in active collusion with police officials ?
17.
Now let me unfurl each of the rival contention urged by the combating parties and view the same in the beacon of light of settled principles of law and materials placed on record.

It is the specific defence of the respondent No.2 that, there is a inordinate delay of 3 months 10 days in setting criminal law into motion and as such the insured vehicle is falsely implicated in this case so as to gulp the compensation amount.
When this being the specific contention of the respondent No.2 herein the onus of proof U/Sec.102 of Indian Evidence Act shifts on the petitioner to explain the cause of delay.
According to the version of the petitioner, the accident had happened on 01.10.2014 at 7.00 p.m.
The contents of Ex.P.2 discloses that the criminal law set into motion by filing FIS on 12.01.2015 at 2:30 PM.
Which means to say there is an inordinate delay of 3 months 12 days was caused in setting SCCH-23 criminal law into motion.

It is vociferously argued by learned counsel for the petitioner that, the cause for delay is ventilated in Ex.P.2 itself wherein the driver of the car assured to reimburse the hospital expenses but he did not do so.
As such the delay of 3 months 12 days was caused.
Much was canvassed by the learned counsel for the petitioner by relying of Ex.P.12 which is said to be intimation given by Fortis Hospital to the jurisdictional police.

On relying of the above said document it is stoutly canvassed that, the intimation was sent on the date of accident itself when such is the case for the lapse on the part of jurisdictional police, the petitioner cannot penalized.
It is relevant to note that, even after the remanded of the petition, the petitioner did not choose to examine the MRT of Fortis Hospital to give evidence with regard to the police intimation also.
The said document is disputed by the respondent No.2 herein.
When such is the case it is the burden bestowed on the petitioner to summon the document from proper custody.
The proper custody is the MRT of Fortis Hospital.
The petitioner before remand had examined the MRT of Fortis Hospital as a PW2 and he got marked Ex.P.20 to 22 documents.
The said MRT who is examined as PW2 did not produce the police intimation or the MLC Extract.
Further on close perusal of Ex.P.12 said SCCH-23 to be the police intimation it bears the seal of one International Hospital Ltd., which does not have any nexus with the Fortis Hospital.
Added more the petitioner did not make any endevour to summon the IO to prove the said police intimation.
In the absence of MLC extract and the police intimation from the proper custody the version of the petitioner cannot be trusted as gospel truth.

sentences.text: Further on perusal of order passed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA-5232/2017 it reflects that the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka had given the liberty to the petitioner to lead evidence.
The petitioner after remand had choose to lead evidence of one Ranjith, who is the said to be eye-witness to the accident.
He during his chief examination had deposed that he had eye-witnessed the accident on 01.10.2014.
Thereafter he was subjected to the litmus test of cross-examination, wherein he categorically admitted that the petitioner was riding the vehicle along with one pillion rider by name Darshan.

Further, his falsity in the evidence is elicited by the respondent No.2 counsel by getting it vital admission which reads as hereunder :
After the lapse of one month from the date of accident I had signed Ex.P.4 Mahazar at the spot.
SCCH-23 19.
This admission has a relevance having regard to the facts of the case.
The FIS itself was filed after 3 months 12 days from the date of accident.
The Ex.P4 mahazar was drawn on 12.01.2015 which means to say on the date of FIS.
When such being the case PW4 attending for the mahazar within 1 month is for from truth.
This court can concede a fact that as the time passes the memory fades.
The said Ranjith is arrayed as CW.3 in Ex.P.7 Chargesheet.
On close perusal of chargesheet it reflects that the said Ranjith is only the Mahazar witness.
He has not at all eye- witness to the accident.
According to the admission of PW1 himself during the course of cross examination that only Darshan and Sunil were present at the time of accident.
The above said admission coupled with the contents of chargesheet clearly discloses clearly discloses that PW.4 has never ever eye-witnessed the accident.
There is absolutely no materials placed on record as to why the inordinate delay of 3 months 12 days was caused.
20. The next lap of contention urged by the petitioner is that, the petitioner was taking treatment in the hospital and as such there was a delay of 3 months 12 days was caused.
When this being the specific contention urged by the petitioners it is relevant to dwell into the medical SCCH-23 records so as to dig out the truth in the case of petitioners.
The petitioner has produced the discharge summary at Ex.P.13.
On close perusal of the discharge summary it reflects that the petitioner was admitted to the Fortis Hospital on 01.10.2014 and he was discharged on 07.10.2014.
On perusal of the said the discharge summary, it reveals that the condition of the petitioner was stable and he was advised with only tablets.
Which means to say the petitioner was in the hospital for only 7 days soon after the accident and thereafter on 11.11.2014 he was again admitted and underwent rotation flap skin grafting.
This categorically reveals that petitioner was under treatment for just 7 to 8 days that too soon after the accident.
The evidence of PW3 being the doctor also plays an important role.
On careful perusal of his evidence it reflects that at the time of discharge also the condition of the petitioner was stable.
Which means to say that after discharge he would have filed a complaint but he did not choose to file any complaint.
Then the question arises in the mind of this court as to what prevented the petitioner to file the complaint.
These questions remain unanswered and untouched.

The next squirt contention urged by the petitioner is that the owner, driver of the car have agreed to bare the medical expenses as such the petitioner did not choose to file any complaint.
In order to substantiate the same absolutely no material are placed before this court.
Even the petitioner has pleaded ignorance as to the name of the driver and owner of the car.
As per the evidence of PW.1 one Sunil had snapped photographs soon after the accident.
But this is contradictory to the statement given by PW.4 who deposed that he was the one who is snapped the photograph.
The said photo is not annexed with CD or any authentication as mandated under Sec.65B of Indian Evidence Act.
The date, time is also not forthcoming from the said photograph.
According to the version of the petitioner he was accompanied by one Darshan who was the pillion rider of the motorcycle, but the petitioner did not choose to examine the said Darshan.
As per the version of the PW1 during the course of cross-examination that one Sunil took snap on the date of accident but the same is given go by by the petitioner by examining PW4.
If really the accident had happened, the petitioner might have made an endeavour to examine the said Sunil and Darshan who are his close friends.
But for the reasons best known to the petitioner, even after the remand, he did not chose to SCCH-23 examine them.
Further, the petitioner has also not examined the hospital authorities or to produce MLC extract.

22. As per Ex.P.22 case sheet the petitioner was taken to the hospital by one Manjunath, who is the relative of the petitioner but according to the PW1, he was taken by his friends, Darshan and Sunil.
According to PW4, he was also present at the place of accident.
These three versions are total contradictory to each other.
The case sheet further discloses that even the petitioner was also conscious.
When such being the case, the question arises in the mind of this court as to what prevented the petitioner to narrate about the manner of accident.
The non-submission of the MLC extract and non-examination of eye-witness is fatal to the case of the petitioner.
23. Further according to the version of the petitioner one Darshan was a pillion rider in the motorcycle on the ill- fated day of accident.
But strangely he was not injured.
Be that as it may, it is not dispute in controversy in the instant petition.
Further PW1 has pleaded his blissful ignorance as to the car number and also which part of the car is damaged.

Another important admission which shook the whole case of the petitioner reads as hereunder :  SCCH-23

24.
This admission when it is viewed in the beacon of light of the reasons assigned by the petitioner for delay in filing FIS it is totally contradictory as per the version of the petitioner.

The car driver and owner had assured the petitioner to provide the medical expenses and as such he did not file any complaint but this admission goes to show that the car driver and owner was sent away without taking their identity details.
This admission shows the falsity of the case of the petitioner.
Viewed from any angle this court does not find any reasons to trust the version of petitioner.
It is a clear case of fraudulent claim made by the petitioner with an intention to get compensation.
The medical records which came into existence, immediately after the accident will prevail over the police documents.
This is a classic case of implicating the insured vehicle in active collusion with police officials.

Further the IMV Report as per Ex.P6 also discloses that there is no absolutely no damage to the insured vehicle.
When such being the case beyond any stretch of imagination it cannot be considered as that insured vehicle involved in the SCCH-23 accident.

sentences.text: Again the the facts of the above cited decision is completely take a diversion from the fact of the instant case on hand.
In the above said decision there was only a delay of 9 days in setting criminal law into motion and the petitioner therein was admitted in the hospital for 13 days.
Moreover the petitioner therein was a Pardanasheen who generally does not have much public exposures.
Having regard to these facts it was held that in the absence of material discredit the charge-sheet the version of the police U/Sec.114 r/w 32 of Evidence Act a presumption was drawn.
But whereas in the instant case of hand there is an void contradictions which cannot be red in harmony and the same is exhaustively discussed above.

sentences.text: Further a critical evaluation of the entire material available on record, proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accident occurred purely on account of fault of the petitioner.

It appears that the police with an intention to help the claimant in getting compensation, built up the case that the petitioner was injured in a Road Traffic SCCH-23 Accident by falsely implant the insured vehicle.
The theory put forth by the petitioner that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of insured car is contrary to the evidence on record.
It is a clear case of fraudulent claim made by the petitioner with an intention to get compensation.
Hence this Tribunal answers issue No.1 in the negative.
30. ISSUE NO.2 :

In view of the findings arrived at issue No.1, the petitioner failed to prove that he had sustained injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of the car bearing Reg.
No.KA-13-B-4541 the involvement of the vehicle is also not proved.
Accordingly the claim is not maintainable.

Consequently issue No.2 deserves to be answered 'In the negative'.
31. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby dismissed with costs.
SCCH-23 Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the injuries caused in a Road Traffic accident.
, at that time the driver of Indica car bearing Reg.No.KA-13-B- 4541 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner so as SCCH-23 to endanger human life and dashed to the vehicle of the petitioner and because of the said accident the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries all over his body.
The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending car and as such, the respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.2 admitting the issuance of SCCH-23 insurance policy in respect of Indica car bearing Reg.No.KA-13-B-4541.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the car did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date Hemanta Kumar K vs Vijayakumar A B on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194723581/
2 of accident.
ISSUES
1 ) Whether the petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in RTA that alleged to have been occurred on 01.10.2014 at about 7:00 p.m., on West of Card Road, near First Block Junction, Rajajinagara and the petitioner sustained injuries due to rash and negligent driving of the Indica car driver, vehicle bearing No.KA-13-B-4541?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as claimed?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
SCCH-23 3) What order or award ?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Hence prayed to dismiss the Hemanta Kumar K vs Vijayakumar A B on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194723581/
4 petition.
15.
It is the specific defence of the respondent No.2 that, there is a inordinate delay of 3 months 10 days in setting criminal law into motion and as such the insured vehicle is falsely implicated in this case so as to gulp the compensation amount.
When this being the specific contention of the respondent No.2 herein the onus of proof U/Sec.102 of Indian Evidence Act shifts on the petitioner to explain the cause of delay.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is relevant to note that, even after the remanded of the petition, the petitioner did not choose to examine the MRT of Fortis Hospital to give evidence with regard to the police intimation also.
When such is the case it is the burden bestowed on the petitioner to summon the document from proper custody.
In the absence of MLC extract and the police intimation from the proper custody the version of the petitioner cannot be trusted as gospel truth.
Hemanta Kumar K vs Vijayakumar A B on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194723581/
5 18.
The evidence of PW3 being the doctor also plays an important role.
On careful perusal of his evidence it reflects that at the time of discharge also the condition of the petitioner was stable.
Which means to say that after discharge he would have filed a complaint but he did not choose to file any complaint.
SCCH-23 Hemanta Kumar K vs Vijayakumar A B
The car driver and owner had assured the petitioner to provide the medical expenses and as such he did not file any complaint but this admission goes to show that the car driver and owner was sent away without taking their identity details.
This admission shows the falsity of the case of the petitioner.
Viewed from any angle this court does not find any reasons to trust the version of petitioner.
It is a clear case of fraudulent claim made by the petitioner with an intention to get compensation.
The medical records which came into existence, immediately after the accident will prevail over the police documents.
This is a classic case of implicating the insured vehicle in active collusion with police officials.
Further respondent No.2 has also relied on decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.No.3263/2014 in case of Manager, National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Gurumurthappa and Another, Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.No.3375/2010 in case of ICICI Lombard GIC V/s Lakshmamma and another, Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.No.4897/2006 in case of Sundresh V/s Bajaj Allianz GIC and another.
27. The petitioners are not entitled for any compensation as the petitioners have failed to prove the involvement of the insured vehicle.
The evidence discloses that insured vehicle is not at all involved in the accident.
But whereas coming to the fact of the instant case there is an inordinate unexplained delay of 3 months 12 days.
Further the IMV Report as per Ex.P6 also discloses that there is no absolutely no damage to the insured vehicle.
When such being the case beyond any stretch of imagination it cannot be considered as that insured vehicle involved in the SCCH-23 accident.
It is a clear case of fraudulent claim made by the petitioner with an intention to get compensation.
Hence this Tribunal answers issue No.1 in the negative.
opennyai_summary.decision:
30. ISSUE NO.2 :
Accordingly the claim is not maintainable.
Consequently issue No.2 deserves to be answered 'In the negative'.
31. ISSUE NO.3 :
In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby dismissed with costs.
SCCH-23 Draw award accordingly.
